[445](https://docs.rs#445)// ── ConformanceMonitor ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[446](https://docs.rs#446)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// ETSI TR 101 290 transport-stream conformance monitor.
[448](https://docs.rs#448)///
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// Feed one TS packet at a time via [`feed`](Self::feed); each call returns
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// the events raised by that packet. The monitor is synchronous and
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// single-threaded — no interior mutability, no async.
[452](https://docs.rs#452)pub struct ConformanceMonitor {
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    config: Config,
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    events: Vec<ConformanceEvent>,
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    stats: Stats,
[456](https://docs.rs#456)
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    // Sync hysteresis state machine (1.1)
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    in_sync: bool,
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    good_run: u8,
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    bad_run: u8,
[461](https://docs.rs#461)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    // Per-PID continuity counter (1.4)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    cc_states: BTreeMap<u16, CcState>,
[464](https://docs.rs#464)
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    // PAT section reassembly + timing (1.3.a)
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    pat_reassembler: SectionReassembler,
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    pat_timer: PresenceTimer,
[468](https://docs.rs#468)
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    // PMT section reassembly + timing per program_map_PID (1.5.a)
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    pmt_trackings: BTreeMap<u16, PmtTracking>,
[471](https://docs.rs#471)
[472](https://docs.rs#472)    // Referenced ES PID timing (1.6)
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    es_trackings: BTreeMap<u16, EsTracking>,
[474](https://docs.rs#474)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    // Well-known SI/PSI section reassembly + CRC checking (2.2)
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    si_reassemblies: BTreeMap<u16, SiReassembly>,
[477](https://docs.rs#477)
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    // Per-PID PCR tracking (2.3a, 2.3b)
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    pcr_states: BTreeMap<u16, PcrState>,
[480](https://docs.rs#480)
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    // Per-PID PTS tracking (2.5)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    pts_states: BTreeMap<u16, PtsState>,
[483](https://docs.rs#483)
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    // CAT tracking (2.6)
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    cat_seen: bool,
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    scrambled_without_cat_reported: bool,
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    // SI repetition-interval timers keyed by table_id (3.2)
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    si_timers: BTreeMap<u8, SiRepetitionTimer>,
[490](https://docs.rs#490)}
[491](https://docs.rs#491)
[492](https://docs.rs#492)impl ConformanceMonitor {
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    /// Create a monitor with default configuration.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)        Self::with_config(Config::default())
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    }
[497](https://docs.rs#497)
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    /// Create a monitor with the given configuration.
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    pub fn with_config(config: Config) -> Self {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        let mut si_reassemblies = BTreeMap::new();
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        for &pid in &SI_PIDS {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)            si_reassemblies.insert(
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                pid,
[504](https://docs.rs#504)                SiReassembly {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                    reassembler: SectionReassembler::default(),
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                },
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            );
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        }
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        Self {
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            config,
[511](https://docs.rs#511)            events: Vec::new(),
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            stats: Stats {
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                packets: 0,
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                events: 0,
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                in_sync: false,
[516](https://docs.rs#516)            },
[517](https://docs.rs#517)            in_sync: false,
[518](https://docs.rs#518)            good_run: 0,
[519](https://docs.rs#519)            bad_run: 0,
[520](https://docs.rs#520)            cc_states: BTreeMap::new(),
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            pat_reassembler: SectionReassembler::default(),
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            pat_timer: PresenceTimer {
[523](https://docs.rs#523)                last_seen: Duration::ZERO,
[524](https://docs.rs#524)                reported: false,
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            },
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            pmt_trackings: BTreeMap::new(),
[527](https://docs.rs#527)            es_trackings: BTreeMap::new(),
[528](https://docs.rs#528)            si_reassemblies,
[529](https://docs.rs#529)            pcr_states: BTreeMap::new(),
[530](https://docs.rs#530)            pts_states: BTreeMap::new(),
[531](https://docs.rs#531)            cat_seen: false,
[532](https://docs.rs#532)            scrambled_without_cat_reported: false,
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            si_timers: BTreeMap::new(),
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        }
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    }
[536](https://docs.rs#536)
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    /// Feed ONE TS packet (any length; 188 expected) with its caller-supplied
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// arrival time `t`.
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    ///
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// `t` must be monotonic non-decreasing across calls (documented but not
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// enforced). Returns the events raised by this packet.
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    pub fn feed(&mut self, ts_packet: &[u8], t: Duration) -> &[ConformanceEvent] {
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        self.events.clear();
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        self.stats.packets += 1;
[545](https://docs.rs#545)
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        // ── Step 2: Sync byte check (1.2) ─────────────────────────────────
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        let sync_ok = !ts_packet.is_empty() && ts_packet[0] == SYNC_BYTE;
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        if !sync_ok {
[549](https://docs.rs#549)            self.emit(Indicator::SyncByteError, None, t, "sync_byte != 0x47");
[550](https://docs.rs#550)        }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        // ── Step 3: Sync hysteresis state machine (1.1) ──────────────────
[553](https://docs.rs#553)        if sync_ok {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)            self.good_run = self.good_run.saturating_add(1);
[555](https://docs.rs#555)            self.bad_run = 0;
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            if !self.in_sync && self.good_run >= self.config.sync_acquire_packets {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                self.in_sync = true;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            }
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        } else {
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            self.bad_run = self.bad_run.saturating_add(1);
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            self.good_run = 0;
[562](https://docs.rs#562)            if self.in_sync && self.bad_run >= self.config.sync_loss_packets {
[563](https://docs.rs#563)                self.in_sync = false;
[564](https://docs.rs#564)                self.emit(
[565](https://docs.rs#565)                    Indicator::TsSyncLoss,
[566](https://docs.rs#566)                    None,
[567](https://docs.rs#567)                    t,
[568](https://docs.rs#568)                    "sync lost after hysteresis threshold",
[569](https://docs.rs#569)                );
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            }
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        }
[572](https://docs.rs#572)
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        // Per the doc: "If indicator 1.1 is activated then all other
[574](https://docs.rs#574)        // indicators are invalid." While not in sync, suppress all other
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        // indicators.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        if !self.in_sync {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)            return &self.events;
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        }
[579](https://docs.rs#579)
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        // ── Step 4: Parse TS packet ───────────────────────────────────────
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        let packet = match TsPacket::parse(ts_packet) {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)            Ok(p) => p,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)            Err(_) => return &self.events,
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        };
[585](https://docs.rs#585)        let header = &packet.header;
[586](https://docs.rs#586)        let pid = header.pid;
[587](https://docs.rs#587)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        // ── 2.1 Transport_error (Table 5.0b indicator 2.1) ──────────────
[589](https://docs.rs#589)        if header.tei {
[590](https://docs.rs#590)            self.emit(
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                Indicator::TransportError,
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                Some(pid),
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                t,
[594](https://docs.rs#594)                format!("transport_error_indicator set on PID 0x{:04X}", pid),
[595](https://docs.rs#595)            );
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        }
[597](https://docs.rs#597)
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        // ── Step 5: Continuity_count_error (1.4) ─────────────────────────
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        if pid != PID_NULL {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            self.check_cc(
[601](https://docs.rs#601)                pid,
[602](https://docs.rs#602)                header.continuity_counter,
[603](https://docs.rs#603)                header.has_payload,
[604](https://docs.rs#604)                t,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)                ts_packet,
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            );
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        }
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        // ── Step 7: PAT_error_2 — scrambling check (1.3.a) ──────────────
[610](https://docs.rs#610)        if pid == PID_PAT && header.scrambling != 0 {
[611](https://docs.rs#611)            self.emit(
[612](https://docs.rs#612)                Indicator::PatError2,
[613](https://docs.rs#613)                Some(PID_PAT),
[614](https://docs.rs#614)                t,
[615](https://docs.rs#615)                format!(
[616](https://docs.rs#616)                    "scrambling_control_field != 00 on PID 0x0000 (got {})",
[617](https://docs.rs#617)                    header.scrambling
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                ),
[619](https://docs.rs#619)            );
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        }
[621](https://docs.rs#621)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        // ── Step 8: PMT_error_2 — scrambling check (1.5.a) ──────────────
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        if self.pmt_trackings.contains_key(&pid) && header.scrambling != 0 {
[624](https://docs.rs#624)            self.emit(
[625](https://docs.rs#625)                Indicator::PmtError2,
[626](https://docs.rs#626)                Some(pid),
[627](https://docs.rs#627)                t,
[628](https://docs.rs#628)                format!(
[629](https://docs.rs#629)                    "scrambling_control_field != 00 on program_map_PID 0x{:04X}",
[630](https://docs.rs#630)                    pid
[631](https://docs.rs#631)                ),
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            );
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        }
[634](https://docs.rs#634)
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        // ── 2.6 CAT_error — scrambled packet with no CAT (Table 5.0b 2.6)
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        //
[637](https://docs.rs#637)        // At stream start, scrambled packets may arrive before a CAT section
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        // has been acquired; this check fires once in that case. It re-arms
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        // (see `check_cat_table_id`) when a CAT later appears, so the error is
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        // re-detectable after a CAT section is seen.
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        if header.scrambling != 0 && !self.cat_seen && !self.scrambled_without_cat_reported {
[642](https://docs.rs#642)            self.scrambled_without_cat_reported = true;
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            self.emit(
[644](https://docs.rs#644)                Indicator::CatError,
[645](https://docs.rs#645)                Some(pid),
[646](https://docs.rs#646)                t,
[647](https://docs.rs#647)                format!(
[648](https://docs.rs#648)                    "scrambled packet on PID 0x{:04X} but no CAT seen on PID 0x0001",
[649](https://docs.rs#649)                    pid
[650](https://docs.rs#650)                ),
[651](https://docs.rs#651)            );
[652](https://docs.rs#652)        }
[653](https://docs.rs#653)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)        // ── Step 6: Section reassembly — PAT ─────────────────────────────
[655](https://docs.rs#655)        if pid == PID_PAT && header.has_payload {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)            if let Some(payload) = packet.payload {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)                self.pat_reassembler.feed(payload, header.pusi);
[658](https://docs.rs#658)            }
[659](https://docs.rs#659)            self.pat_timer.last_seen = t;
[660](https://docs.rs#660)            self.pat_timer.reported = false;
[661](https://docs.rs#661)            while let Some(section_bytes) = self.pat_reassembler.pop_section() {
[662](https://docs.rs#662)                self.check_crc_and_process_pat(§ion_bytes, pid, t);
[663](https://docs.rs#663)            }
[664](https://docs.rs#664)        }
[665](https://docs.rs#665)
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        // ── Step 6b: Section reassembly — PMT PIDs ───────────────────────
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        if self.pmt_trackings.contains_key(&pid) && header.has_payload {
[668](https://docs.rs#668)            if let Some(payload) = packet.payload {
[669](https://docs.rs#669)                if let Some(tracking) = self.pmt_trackings.get_mut(&pid) {
[670](https://docs.rs#670)                    tracking.reassembler.feed(payload, header.pusi);
[671](https://docs.rs#671)                }
[672](https://docs.rs#672)            }
[673](https://docs.rs#673)            let sections: Vec<_> = if let Some(tracking) = self.pmt_trackings.get_mut(&pid) {
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                tracking.timer.last_seen = t;
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                tracking.timer.reported = false;
[676](https://docs.rs#676)                core::iter::from_fn(|| tracking.reassembler.pop_section()).collect()
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            } else {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)                Vec::new()
[679](https://docs.rs#679)            };
[680](https://docs.rs#680)            for section_bytes in §ions {
[681](https://docs.rs#681)                self.check_crc_and_process_pmt(section_bytes, pid, t);
[682](https://docs.rs#682)            }
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        }
[684](https://docs.rs#684)
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        // ── Step 6c: Section reassembly — well-known SI/PSI PIDs (2.2) ───
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        // PAT and PMT PIDs are handled above (they have separate reassembly
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        // for P1 logic). Only process the non-PAT, non-PMT SI PIDs here.
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        if pid != PID_PAT
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            && !self.pmt_trackings.contains_key(&pid)
[690](https://docs.rs#690)            && self.si_reassemblies.contains_key(&pid)
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            && header.has_payload
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        {
[693](https://docs.rs#693)            if let Some(payload) = packet.payload {
[694](https://docs.rs#694)                if let Some(si_ra) = self.si_reassemblies.get_mut(&pid) {
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                    si_ra.reassembler.feed(payload, header.pusi);
[696](https://docs.rs#696)                }
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            }
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            let sections: Vec<_> = if let Some(si_ra) = self.si_reassemblies.get_mut(&pid) {
[699](https://docs.rs#699)                core::iter::from_fn(|| si_ra.reassembler.pop_section()).collect()
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            } else {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)                Vec::new()
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            };
[703](https://docs.rs#703)            for section_bytes in §ions {
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                self.check_crc_for_si(section_bytes, pid, t);
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                self.check_cat_table_id(section_bytes, pid, t);
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                self.update_si_repetition(section_bytes, pid, t);
[707](https://docs.rs#707)            }
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        }
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        // Also CRC-check completed PAT/PMT sections via the si_reassemblies
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        // map (these share the same PID). PAT and PMT already have their own
[711](https://docs.rs#711)        // reassemblers above — the si_reassemblies entries for those PIDs are
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        // not fed again. CRC checking for PAT/PMT is done inside
[713](https://docs.rs#713)        // check_crc_and_process_pat / check_crc_and_process_pmt.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        // ── Step 9: PID_error — update last_seen for referenced PIDs ─────
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        if let Some(tracking) = self.es_trackings.get_mut(&pid) {
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            tracking.timer.last_seen = t;
[718](https://docs.rs#718)            tracking.timer.reported = false;
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        }
[720](https://docs.rs#720)
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        // ── 2.3a / 2.3b: PCR checks (Table 5.0b indicators 2.3a, 2.3b) ──
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        if let Some(Ok(af)) = packet.adaptation_field() {
[723](https://docs.rs#723)            if let Some(pcr) = af.pcr {
[724](https://docs.rs#724)                self.check_pcr(pid, pcr.as_27mhz(), af.discontinuity_indicator, t);
[725](https://docs.rs#725)            }
[726](https://docs.rs#726)        }
[727](https://docs.rs#727)
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        // ── 2.5: PTS check (Table 5.0b indicator 2.5) ───────────────────
[729](https://docs.rs#729)        if header.pusi
[730](https://docs.rs#730)            && header.scrambling == 0
[731](https://docs.rs#731)            && self.es_trackings.contains_key(&pid)
[732](https://docs.rs#732)            && header.has_payload
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        {
[734](https://docs.rs#734)            if let Some(payload) = packet.payload {
[735](https://docs.rs#735)                self.check_pts(pid, payload, t);
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            }
[737](https://docs.rs#737)        }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)
[739](https://docs.rs#739)        // ── Presence-timeout evaluation (1.3.a, 1.5.a, 1.6) ────────────
[740](https://docs.rs#740)        self.check_presence_timeouts(t);
[741](https://docs.rs#741)
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        &self.events
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    }
[744](https://docs.rs#744)
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    /// Diagnostic counters.
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    pub fn stats(&self) -> Stats {
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        Stats {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)            in_sync: self.in_sync,
[749](https://docs.rs#749)            ..self.stats
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        }
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    }
[752](https://docs.rs#752)
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    // ── Internal helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
[754](https://docs.rs#754)
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    fn emit(
[756](https://docs.rs#756)        &mut self,
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        indicator: Indicator,
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        pid: Option<u16>,
[759](https://docs.rs#759)        at: Duration,
[760](https://docs.rs#760)        detail: impl Into<String>,
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ) {
[762](https://docs.rs#762)        let event = ConformanceEvent {
[763](https://docs.rs#763)            indicator,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)            priority: indicator.priority(),
[765](https://docs.rs#765)            pid,
[766](https://docs.rs#766)            at,
[767](https://docs.rs#767)            detail: detail.into(),
[768](https://docs.rs#768)        };
[769](https://docs.rs#769)        self.stats.events += 1;
[770](https://docs.rs#770)        self.events.push(event);
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    }
[772](https://docs.rs#772)
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    /// Continuity_count_error (1.4) check.
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    fn check_cc(&mut self, pid: u16, cc: u8, has_payload: bool, t: Duration, raw: &[u8]) {
[775](https://docs.rs#775)        // Check for discontinuity_indicator in the adaptation field BEFORE
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        // mutating cc_states (avoids holding the entry borrow across self.emit).
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        let discontinuity = if raw.len() >= 5 {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            let b3 = raw[3];
[779](https://docs.rs#779)            let has_adaptation = (b3 & 0x20) != 0;
[780](https://docs.rs#780)            if has_adaptation {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)                let af_len = raw[4] as usize;
[782](https://docs.rs#782)                if af_len > 0 && raw.len() > 5 {
[783](https://docs.rs#783)                    (raw[5] & 0x80) != 0
[784](https://docs.rs#784)                } else {
[785](https://docs.rs#785)                    false
[786](https://docs.rs#786)                }
[787](https://docs.rs#787)            } else {
[788](https://docs.rs#788)                false
[789](https://docs.rs#789)            }
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        } else {
[791](https://docs.rs#791)            false
[792](https://docs.rs#792)        };
[793](https://docs.rs#793)
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        // Compute what we need from the existing state, then decide.
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        let (expected, is_duplicate, should_emit_dup, should_emit_cc) = {
[796](https://docs.rs#796)            let state = self.cc_states.entry(pid).or_insert_with(|| CcState {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)                last_cc: cc,
[798](https://docs.rs#798)                had_payload: has_payload,
[799](https://docs.rs#799)                dup_used: false,
[800](https://docs.rs#800)                initialised: false,
[801](https://docs.rs#801)            });
[802](https://docs.rs#802)
[803](https://docs.rs#803)            if !state.initialised {
[804](https://docs.rs#804)                state.last_cc = cc;
[805](https://docs.rs#805)                state.had_payload = has_payload;
[806](https://docs.rs#806)                state.dup_used = false;
[807](https://docs.rs#807)                state.initialised = true;
[808](https://docs.rs#808)                return;
[809](https://docs.rs#809)            }
[810](https://docs.rs#810)
[811](https://docs.rs#811)            if discontinuity {
[812](https://docs.rs#812)                // Will update state below — just signal no emit.
[813](https://docs.rs#813)                (0u8, false, false, false)
[814](https://docs.rs#814)            } else {
[815](https://docs.rs#815)                let is_duplicate = cc == state.last_cc && has_payload;
[816](https://docs.rs#816)                let mut should_emit_dup = false;
[817](https://docs.rs#817)                let mut should_emit_cc = false;
[818](https://docs.rs#818)
[819](https://docs.rs#819)                if is_duplicate {
[820](https://docs.rs#820)                    if state.dup_used {
[821](https://docs.rs#821)                        should_emit_dup = true;
[822](https://docs.rs#822)                    }
[823](https://docs.rs#823)                } else {
[824](https://docs.rs#824)                    state.dup_used = false;
[825](https://docs.rs#825)                    let expected = if has_payload {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)                        (state.last_cc.wrapping_add(1)) & 0x0F
[827](https://docs.rs#827)                    } else {
[828](https://docs.rs#828)                        state.last_cc
[829](https://docs.rs#829)                    };
[830](https://docs.rs#830)                    if cc != expected {
[831](https://docs.rs#831)                        should_emit_cc = true;
[832](https://docs.rs#832)                    }
[833](https://docs.rs#833)                }
[834](https://docs.rs#834)
[835](https://docs.rs#835)                (
[836](https://docs.rs#836)                    if has_payload {
[837](https://docs.rs#837)                        (state.last_cc.wrapping_add(1)) & 0x0F
[838](https://docs.rs#838)                    } else {
[839](https://docs.rs#839)                        state.last_cc
[840](https://docs.rs#840)                    },
[841](https://docs.rs#841)                    is_duplicate,
[842](https://docs.rs#842)                    should_emit_dup,
[843](https://docs.rs#843)                    should_emit_cc,
[844](https://docs.rs#844)                )
[845](https://docs.rs#845)            }
[846](https://docs.rs#846)        };
[847](https://docs.rs#847)
[848](https://docs.rs#848)        // Now emit events without holding a borrow on cc_states.
[849](https://docs.rs#849)        if should_emit_dup {
[850](https://docs.rs#850)            self.emit(
[851](https://docs.rs#851)                Indicator::ContinuityCountError,
[852](https://docs.rs#852)                Some(pid),
[853](https://docs.rs#853)                t,
[854](https://docs.rs#854)                format!(
[855](https://docs.rs#855)                    "second consecutive duplicate on PID 0x{:04X} (cc={})",
[856](https://docs.rs#856)                    pid, cc
[857](https://docs.rs#857)                ),
[858](https://docs.rs#858)            );
[859](https://docs.rs#859)        }
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        if should_emit_cc {
[861](https://docs.rs#861)            self.emit(
[862](https://docs.rs#862)                Indicator::ContinuityCountError,
[863](https://docs.rs#863)                Some(pid),
[864](https://docs.rs#864)                t,
[865](https://docs.rs#865)                format!("expected cc={}, got {} on PID 0x{:04X}", expected, cc, pid),
[866](https://docs.rs#866)            );
[867](https://docs.rs#867)        }
[868](https://docs.rs#868)
[869](https://docs.rs#869)        // Finally, update state.
[870](https://docs.rs#870)        let state = self.cc_states.get_mut(&pid).unwrap();
[871](https://docs.rs#871)        if discontinuity {
[872](https://docs.rs#872)            state.last_cc = cc;
[873](https://docs.rs#873)            state.had_payload = has_payload;
[874](https://docs.rs#874)            state.dup_used = false;
[875](https://docs.rs#875)        } else if is_duplicate {
[876](https://docs.rs#876)            // First duplicate is legal; mark dup_used but do NOT update last_cc.
[877](https://docs.rs#877)            state.dup_used = true;
[878](https://docs.rs#878)        } else {
[879](https://docs.rs#879)            state.dup_used = false;
[880](https://docs.rs#880)            state.last_cc = cc;
[881](https://docs.rs#881)            state.had_payload = has_payload;
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        }
[883](https://docs.rs#883)    }
[884](https://docs.rs#884)
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    /// CRC-check a completed section and, if on PID_PAT, process it.
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    fn check_crc_and_process_pat(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[887](https://docs.rs#887)        // 2.2: CRC check on PAT section.
[888](https://docs.rs#888)        self.check_crc_for_section(section_bytes, pid, t);
[889](https://docs.rs#889)
[890](https://docs.rs#890)        self.process_pat_section(section_bytes, t);
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    }
[892](https://docs.rs#892)
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    /// CRC-check a completed section and, if on a PMT PID, process it.
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    fn check_crc_and_process_pmt(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[895](https://docs.rs#895)        // 2.2: CRC check on PMT section.
[896](https://docs.rs#896)        self.check_crc_for_section(section_bytes, pid, t);
[897](https://docs.rs#897)
[898](https://docs.rs#898)        self.process_pmt_section(section_bytes, pid, t);
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    }
[900](https://docs.rs#900)
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// TR 101 290 v1.4.1 Table 5.0b indicator 2.2 — CRC_error.
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    ///
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    /// On any tracked PID, if a completed long-form section has a CRC
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    /// mismatch, emit `CrcError`.
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    fn check_crc_for_section(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[906](https://docs.rs#906)        let section = match Section::parse(section_bytes) {
[907](https://docs.rs#907)            Ok(s) => s,
[908](https://docs.rs#908)            Err(_) => return,
[909](https://docs.rs#909)        };
[910](https://docs.rs#910)
[911](https://docs.rs#911)        // validate_crc returns Ok for short-form sections (no CRC to check).
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        if let Err(mpeg_ts::error::Error::CrcMismatch { .. }) = section.validate_crc(section_bytes)
[913](https://docs.rs#913)        {
[914](https://docs.rs#914)            self.emit(
[915](https://docs.rs#915)                Indicator::CrcError,
[916](https://docs.rs#916)                Some(pid),
[917](https://docs.rs#917)                t,
[918](https://docs.rs#918)                format!(
[919](https://docs.rs#919)                    "CRC-32 mismatch on PID 0x{:04X} (table_id 0x{:02X})",
[920](https://docs.rs#920)                    pid, section.table_id
[921](https://docs.rs#921)                ),
[922](https://docs.rs#922)            );
[923](https://docs.rs#923)        }
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    }
[925](https://docs.rs#925)
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    /// CRC-check for SI PIDs that are not PAT/PMT (handled via si_reassemblies).
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    fn check_crc_for_si(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[928](https://docs.rs#928)        self.check_crc_for_section(section_bytes, pid, t);
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    }
[930](https://docs.rs#930)
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    /// TR 101 290 v1.4.1 Table 5.0b indicator 2.6 — CAT_error, condition 1:
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// section with `table_id != 0x01` on PID_CAT.
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    fn check_cat_table_id(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[934](https://docs.rs#934)        if pid != PID_CAT {
[935](https://docs.rs#935)            return;
[936](https://docs.rs#936)        }
[937](https://docs.rs#937)        let section = match Section::parse(section_bytes) {
[938](https://docs.rs#938)            Ok(s) => s,
[939](https://docs.rs#939)            Err(_) => return,
[940](https://docs.rs#940)        };
[941](https://docs.rs#941)        if section.table_id == CAT_TABLE_ID {
[942](https://docs.rs#942)            // Valid CAT section — mark as seen.
[943](https://docs.rs#943)            self.cat_seen = true;
[944](https://docs.rs#944)            // Re-arm the "scrambled without CAT" check so that if a CAT was
[945](https://docs.rs#945)            // previously absent and then appears, the check resets.
[946](https://docs.rs#946)            self.scrambled_without_cat_reported = false;
[947](https://docs.rs#947)        } else {
[948](https://docs.rs#948)            self.emit(
[949](https://docs.rs#949)                Indicator::CatError,
[950](https://docs.rs#950)                Some(PID_CAT),
[951](https://docs.rs#951)                t,
[952](https://docs.rs#952)                format!(
[953](https://docs.rs#953)                    "section with table_id 0x{:02X} on PID 0x0001 (expected 0x01 for CAT)",
[954](https://docs.rs#954)                    section.table_id
[955](https://docs.rs#955)                ),
[956](https://docs.rs#956)            );
[957](https://docs.rs#957)        }
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    }
[959](https://docs.rs#959)
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    /// Process a completed section on PID_PAT.
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    fn process_pat_section(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], t: Duration) {
[962](https://docs.rs#962)        let section = match Section::parse(section_bytes) {
[963](https://docs.rs#963)            Ok(s) => s,
[964](https://docs.rs#964)            Err(_) => return,
[965](https://docs.rs#965)        };
[966](https://docs.rs#966)
[967](https://docs.rs#967)        // 1.3.a: section with table_id other than 0x00 found on PID 0x0000.
[968](https://docs.rs#968)        if section.table_id != PAT_TABLE_ID {
[969](https://docs.rs#969)            self.emit(
[970](https://docs.rs#970)                Indicator::PatError2,
[971](https://docs.rs#971)                Some(PID_PAT),
[972](https://docs.rs#972)                t,
[973](https://docs.rs#973)                format!(
[974](https://docs.rs#974)                    "section with table_id 0x{:02X} on PID 0x0000 (expected 0x00)",
[975](https://docs.rs#975)                    section.table_id
[976](https://docs.rs#976)                ),
[977](https://docs.rs#977)            );
[978](https://docs.rs#978)            return;
[979](https://docs.rs#979)        }
[980](https://docs.rs#980)
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        // Parse the PAT proper.
[982](https://docs.rs#982)        let pat = match PatSection::parse(section_bytes) {
[983](https://docs.rs#983)            Ok(p) => p,
[984](https://docs.rs#984)            Err(_) => return,
[985](https://docs.rs#985)        };
[986](https://docs.rs#986)
[987](https://docs.rs#987)        // Discover program_map_PIDs and start tracking them.
[988](https://docs.rs#988)        for entry in pat.programmes() {
[989](https://docs.rs#989)            let pmt_pid = entry.pid;
[990](https://docs.rs#990)            self.pmt_trackings
[991](https://docs.rs#991)                .entry(pmt_pid)
[992](https://docs.rs#992)                .or_insert_with(|| PmtTracking {
[993](https://docs.rs#993)                    timer: PresenceTimer {
[994](https://docs.rs#994)                        last_seen: t,
[995](https://docs.rs#995)                        reported: false,
[996](https://docs.rs#996)                    },
[997](https://docs.rs#997)                    reassembler: SectionReassembler::default(),
[998](https://docs.rs#998)                });
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        }
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    }
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)    /// Process a completed section on a program_map_PID.
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    fn process_pmt_section(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], _pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)        let section = match Section::parse(section_bytes) {
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)            Ok(s) => s,
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)            Err(_) => return,
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)        };
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)        // 1.5.a only checks presence and scrambling of table_id 0x02 sections.
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)        // If table_id is not 0x02, skip — we don't emit PMT_error_2 for a
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)        // wrong table_id on a program_map_PID (that's not in the spec for
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)        // 1.5.a).
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)        let pmt_table_id: u8 = dvb_si::tables::pmt::TABLE_ID;
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)        if section.table_id != pmt_table_id {
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)            return;
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)        }
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)        // Parse the PMT proper.
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)        let pmt = match PmtSection::parse(section_bytes) {
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)            Ok(p) => p,
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)            Err(_) => return,
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)        };
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)        // Collect new ES PIDs to add.
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)        let mut new_es_pids: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        if pmt.pcr_pid != PID_NULL && !self.es_trackings.contains_key(&pmt.pcr_pid) {
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)            new_es_pids.push(pmt.pcr_pid);
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        }
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        for stream in &pmt.streams {
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)            let es_pid = stream.elementary_pid;
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)            if !self.es_trackings.contains_key(&es_pid) {
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)                new_es_pids.push(es_pid);
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)            }
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)        }
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)        for es_pid in new_es_pids {
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)            self.es_trackings.insert(
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)                es_pid,
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)                EsTracking {
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)                    timer: PresenceTimer {
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)                        last_seen: t,
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)                        reported: false,
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)                    },
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)                },
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)            );
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)        }
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)    }
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)    /// TR 101 290 v1.4.1 Table 5.0b indicators 2.3a / 2.3b — PCR checks.
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)    fn check_pcr(&mut self, pid: u16, pcr_27mhz: u64, discontinuity: bool, t: Duration) {
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)        let state = self.pcr_states.entry(pid).or_insert_with(|| PcrState {
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)            last_pcr_27mhz: 0,
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)            last_pcr_time: Duration::ZERO,
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)            initialised: false,
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)        });
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)        if !state.initialised {
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)            state.last_pcr_27mhz = pcr_27mhz;
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)            state.last_pcr_time = t;
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)            state.initialised = true;
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)            return;
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)        }
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)        // Snapshot state for decision-making before any emit.
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)        let last_pcr_time = state.last_pcr_time;
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)        let last_pcr_27mhz = state.last_pcr_27mhz;
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)        // 2.3a: PCR_repetition_error — interval between consecutive PCR
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)        // values exceeds the configured limit.
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)        let rep_interval = t.saturating_sub(last_pcr_time);
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)        let should_emit_rep = rep_interval > self.config.pcr_repetition_limit;
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)        // 2.3b: PCR_discontinuity_indicator_error — PCR delta exceeds 100 ms
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)        // without a signalled discontinuity.
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)        let delta =
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)            (pcr_27mhz.wrapping_add(PCR_MODULUS_27MHZ) - last_pcr_27mhz) % PCR_MODULUS_27MHZ;
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)        let delta_ms = delta * 1000 / CLOCK_27MHZ;
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)        let limit_ms = self.config.pcr_discontinuity_limit.as_millis() as u64;
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)        let should_emit_disc = delta_ms > limit_ms && !discontinuity;
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)        // Emit outside the HashMap borrow.
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)        if should_emit_rep {
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)            self.emit(
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)                Indicator::PcrRepetitionError,
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)                Some(pid),
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)                t,
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)                format!(
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)                    "PCR interval {} ms exceeds limit {} ms on PID 0x{:04X}",
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)                    rep_interval.as_millis(),
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)                    self.config.pcr_repetition_limit.as_millis(),
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)                    pid
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)                ),
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)            );
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)        }
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)        if should_emit_disc {
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)            self.emit(
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)                Indicator::PcrDiscontinuityError,
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)                Some(pid),
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)                t,
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)                format!(
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)                    "PCR delta {} ms exceeds limit {} ms on PID 0x{:04X} without discontinuity_indicator",
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)                    delta_ms, limit_ms, pid
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)                ),
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)            );
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)        }
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)        // Update state.
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        let state = self.pcr_states.get_mut(&pid).unwrap();
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        state.last_pcr_27mhz = pcr_27mhz;
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)        state.last_pcr_time = t;
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)    }
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)    /// TR 101 290 v1.4.1 Table 5.0b indicator 2.5 — PTS_error.
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)    ///
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)    /// Peeks the PES header on an elementary-stream PID for PTS_DTS_flags.
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)    /// Only checks PIDs that have been "armed" by seeing at least one PTS.
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)    fn check_pts(&mut self, pid: u16, payload: &[u8], t: Duration) {
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)        // PES start-code prefix: 00 00 01.
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)        if payload.len() < PES_FLAGS_OFFSET + 2 {
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)            return;
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)        }
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)        if payload[0] != PES_PREFIX_0 || payload[1] != PES_PREFIX_1 || payload[2] != PES_PREFIX_2 {
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)            return;
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)        }
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)        // Byte 6: `'10' + flags` — the top two bits must be `10`.
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)        let flags_byte = payload[PES_FLAGS_OFFSET];
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)        if (flags_byte >> 6) != 0b10 {
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)            return;
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)        }
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)        // Byte 7: PTS_DTS_flags in bits `[7:6]`.
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)        let pts_dts_flags = payload[PES_FLAGS_OFFSET + 1] & PES_PTS_DTS_FLAGS_MASK;
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)        let pts_present = (pts_dts_flags & PES_PTS_PRESENT) != 0;
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)        if !pts_present {
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)            return;
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)        }
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)        let state = self.pts_states.entry(pid).or_insert_with(|| PtsState {
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)            last_pts_time: Duration::ZERO,
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)            armed: false,
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)        });
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)        if !state.armed {
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)            // First PTS on this PID — arm the check, no error yet.
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)            state.last_pts_time = t;
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)            state.armed = true;
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)            return;
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        }
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)        // Snapshot state for decision-making before any emit.
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        let last_pts_time = state.last_pts_time;
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)        let pts_interval = t.saturating_sub(last_pts_time);
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)        let should_emit = pts_interval > self.config.pts_repetition_limit;
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)        if should_emit {
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)            self.emit(
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)                Indicator::PtsError,
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)                Some(pid),
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)                t,
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)                format!(
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)                    "PTS interval {} ms exceeds limit {} ms on PID 0x{:04X}",
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)                    pts_interval.as_millis(),
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)                    self.config.pts_repetition_limit.as_millis(),
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)                    pid
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)                ),
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)            );
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)        }
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)        // Update state.
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)        let state = self.pts_states.get_mut(&pid).unwrap();
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)        state.last_pts_time = t;
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)    }
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)    /// TR 101 290 v1.4.1 Table 5.0c indicator 3.2 — update SI repetition timer
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)    /// when a completed section on a well-known SI PID matches one of the four
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)    /// tracked table_ids.
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)    fn update_si_repetition(&mut self, section_bytes: &[u8], _pid: u16, t: Duration) {
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)        let table_id = match Section::parse(section_bytes) {
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)            Ok(s) => s.table_id,
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)            Err(_) => return,
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)        };
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)        let is_tracked = table_id == NIT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)            || table_id == SDT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)            || table_id == EIT_PF_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)            || table_id == TDT_TABLE_ID;
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)        if !is_tracked {
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)            return;
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)        }
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)        let timer = self
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)            .si_timers
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)            .entry(table_id)
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)            .or_insert_with(|| SiRepetitionTimer {
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)                last_seen: Duration::ZERO,
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)                reported: false,
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)                armed: false,
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)            });
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)        timer.last_seen = t;
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)        timer.reported = false;
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)        timer.armed = true;
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)    }
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)    /// Evaluate all presence/absence timeouts against the current time `t`.
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)    fn check_presence_timeouts(&mut self, t: Duration) {
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)        // 1.3.a: PAT presence timeout
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)        if t.saturating_sub(self.pat_timer.last_seen) > self.config.pat_max_interval
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)            && !self.pat_timer.reported
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)        {
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)            self.pat_timer.reported = true;
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)            self.emit(
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)                Indicator::PatError2,
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)                Some(PID_PAT),
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)                t,
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)                format!(
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)                    "no PAT section within {} ms",
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)                    self.config.pat_max_interval.as_millis()
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)                ),
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)            );
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)        }
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)        // 1.5.a: PMT presence timeout per program_map_PID
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)        // Collect PIDs that need events, then emit outside the iteration.
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)        let pmt_timeouts: Vec<(u16, u64)> = self
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)            .pmt_trackings
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)            .iter()
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)            .filter_map(|(&pid, tracking)| {
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)                if t.saturating_sub(tracking.timer.last_seen) > self.config.pmt_max_interval
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)                    && !tracking.timer.reported
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)                {
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)                    Some((pid, self.config.pmt_max_interval.as_millis() as u64))
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)                } else {
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)                    None
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)                }
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)            })
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)            .collect();
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)        for (pid, interval_ms) in pmt_timeouts {
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)            if let Some(tracking) = self.pmt_trackings.get_mut(&pid) {
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)                tracking.timer.reported = true;
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)            }
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)            self.emit(
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)                Indicator::PmtError2,
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)                Some(pid),
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)                t,
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)                format!(
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)                    "no PMT section on program_map_PID 0x{:04X} within {} ms",
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)                    pid, interval_ms
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)                ),
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)            );
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)        }
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)        // 1.6: PID_error — referenced PID absence
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)        let pid_timeouts: Vec<(u16, u64)> = self
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)            .es_trackings
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)            .iter()
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)            .filter_map(|(&pid, tracking)| {
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)                if t.saturating_sub(tracking.timer.last_seen) > self.config.pid_error_period
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)                    && !tracking.timer.reported
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)                {
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)                    Some((pid, self.config.pid_error_period.as_secs()))
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)                } else {
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)                    None
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)                }
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)            })
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)            .collect();
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)        for (pid, period_secs) in pid_timeouts {
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)            if let Some(tracking) = self.es_trackings.get_mut(&pid) {
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)                tracking.timer.reported = true;
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)            }
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)            self.emit(
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)                Indicator::PidError,
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)                Some(pid),
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)                t,
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)                format!(
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)                    "referenced PID 0x{:04X} absent for > {} s",
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)                    pid, period_secs
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)                ),
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)            );
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)        }
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)        // 3.2: SI_repetition_error — maximum interval for tracked SI tables.
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)        // Collect table_ids that need events, then emit outside the iteration.
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)        let si_timeouts: Vec<(u8, u64, u16, u64)> = self
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)            .si_timers
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)            .iter()
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)            .filter_map(|(&table_id, timer)| {
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)                if !timer.armed || timer.reported {
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)                    return None;
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)                }
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)                let (limit, pid) = match table_id {
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)                    NIT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => (self.config.si_nit_interval, PID_NIT),
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)                    SDT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => (self.config.si_sdt_interval, PID_SDT_BAT),
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)                    EIT_PF_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => (self.config.si_eit_pf_interval, PID_EIT),
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)                    TDT_TABLE_ID => (self.config.si_tdt_interval, PID_TDT_TOT),
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)                    _ => return None,
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)                };
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)                let interval = t.saturating_sub(timer.last_seen);
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)                if interval > limit {
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)                    Some((
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)                        table_id,
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)                        interval.as_millis() as u64,
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)                        pid,
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)                        limit.as_millis() as u64,
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)                    ))
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)                } else {
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)                    None
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)                }
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)            })
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)            .collect();
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)        for (table_id, interval_ms, pid, limit_ms) in si_timeouts {
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)            if let Some(timer) = self.si_timers.get_mut(&table_id) {
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)                timer.reported = true;
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)            }
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)            let table_name = match table_id {
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)                NIT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => "NIT_actual",
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)                SDT_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => "SDT_actual",
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)                EIT_PF_ACTUAL_TABLE_ID => "EIT_P/F_actual",
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)                TDT_TABLE_ID => "TDT",
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)                _ => "unknown",
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)            };
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)            self.emit(
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)                Indicator::SiRepetitionError,
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)                Some(pid),
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)                t,
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)                format!(
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)                    "{} repetition interval {} ms exceeds {} ms",
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)                    table_name, interval_ms, limit_ms
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)                ),
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)            );
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)        }
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)    }
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)}
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)impl Default for ConformanceMonitor {
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)    fn default() -> Self {
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)        Self::new()
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)    }
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)}

# ConformanceMonitor in dvb_conformance - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-conformance/8.2.1/dvb_conformance/struct.ConformanceMonitor.html

`pub struct ConformanceMonitor { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

ETSI TR 101 290 transport-stream conformance monitor.

Feed one TS packet at a time via [ feed](https://docs.rs/struct.ConformanceMonitor.html#method.feed); each call returns
the events raised by that packet. The monitor is synchronous and
single-threaded — no interior mutability, no async.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/dvb_conformance/lib.rs.html#542-743)#### pub fn [feed](https://docs.rs#method.feed)(&mut self, ts_packet: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], t: [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)) -> &[[ConformanceEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.ConformanceEvent.html)]

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/dvb_conformance/lib.rs.html#542-743)

#### pub fn [feed](https://docs.rs#method.feed)(&mut self, ts_packet: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], t: [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)) -> &[[ConformanceEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.ConformanceEvent.html)]

Feed ONE TS packet (any length; 188 expected) with its caller-supplied
arrival time `t`.

`t` must be monotonic non-decreasing across calls (documented but not
enforced). Returns the events raised by this packet.

# dvb-t2mi 8.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1

# dvb-t2mi

Complete, spec-compliant **ETSI TS 102 773 v1.4.1** DVB-T2 Modulator Interface (T2-MI) parser and builder in Rust.

## What is T2-MI?

T2-MI is the protocol between a DVB-T2 Gateway and a DVB-T2 modulator. It carries:

- **Baseband Frames (BBFRAME)**— the actual DVB-T2 user data
- **L1 signalling**— configuration for each T2 frame (L1-pre and L1-post)
- **Auxiliary I/Q data**— pilot and correction cell values
- **DVB-T2 timestamps**— SFN synchronisation
- **Future Extension Frames (FEF)**— composite signal support (e.g. T2-Base + T2-Lite)

Each T2-MI packet is a 6-byte header + variable payload + 4-byte CRC-32, encapsulated in MPEG-2 TS via data piping.

## Quick start

```
use T2miPump;
use AnyPayload;
let mut pump = new;       // T2-MI PID from the PMT
for packet in ts_packets
```
For un-encapsulated `.t2mi` byte streams use `T2miPump::raw()` + `feed_raw`. The
[ dvb-tools t2mi](https://docs.rs/dvb-tools/) CLI is the complete wrapper
(

`cargo run -p dvb-tools -- t2mi file.ts [--pid 0xNNN|raw] [--inner] [--plp N]`).### Inner-TS recovery in one call

[`inner_ts::InnerTsRecovery`] folds the full chain (T2miPump → `AnyPayload::Bbframe` →
`Bbheader` → `CarryOverExtractor`, NM/HEM + carry-over) into a single
feed-and-collect driver — feed outer TS packets, get inner TS packets out:

```
#
```
`InnerTsRecovery::with_plp(pid, plp_id)` filters to a single PLP.

## What's implemented

### Packet types — all 12 (ETSI TS 102 773 Table 1)

All 12 are in the `declare_payloads!` list in `payload/any.rs`; each has a
`Parse` + `Serialize` impl and round-trip tests. The `AnyPayload` dispatcher
routes every packet type to its typed struct; unknown/reserved values fall
through to `AnyPayload::Unknown` with raw bytes preserved.

| Value | Packet type | Struct |
|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | Baseband Frame — §5.2.1 | `BbframePayload` |
| 0x01 | Auxiliary stream I/Q data — §5.2.2 | `AuxIqPayload` |
| 0x02 | Arbitrary cell insertion — §5.2.3 | `ArbitraryCellsPayload` |
| 0x10 | L1-current signalling — §5.2.4 | `L1CurrentPayload` |
| 0x11 | L1-future signalling — §5.2.5 | `L1FuturePayload` |
| 0x12 | P2 bias balancing cells — §5.2.6 | `P2BiasPayload` |
| 0x20 | DVB-T2 timestamp — §5.2.7 | `T2TimestampPayload` |
| 0x21 | Individual addressing — §5.2.8 | `IndividualAddressingPayload` |
| 0x30 | FEF part: Null — §5.2.9 | `FefNullPayload` |
| 0x31 | FEF part: I/Q data — §5.2.10 | `FefIqPayload` |
| 0x32 | FEF part: composite — §5.2.11 | `FefCompositePayload` |
| 0x33 | FEF sub-part — §5.2.12 | `FefSubPartPayload` |

### L1 signalling (EN 302 755 §7.2)

`L1CurrentPayload` and `L1FuturePayload` expose typed `l1_pre()` / `l1_post()`
accessors that parse the L1-pre and L1-post signalling structures directly from
the payload bytes. Decoded enums (`L1PreType`, `Papr`, `S1Field`, `S2Field`,
`FftMode`, `Gi`, `Pp`, `Mimo`, etc.) live in `payload::l1::enums`.

### DVB-T2 timestamp decoded accessors

`T2TimestampPayload` exposes `emission_offset()` (per-bandwidth `T_sub` units,
§5.2.7 Table 4) and the `is_null` / `is_relative` flags. The `chrono` feature
adds a `utc_emission_time()` accessor returning `DateTime<Utc>`.

### PLP filter

`T2miPump::new(pid)` passes all PLPs through; `InnerTsRecovery::with_plp(pid, plp_id)` restricts the inner-TS recovery to a single PLP. The `T2miEvent`
exposes `plp_id()` for caller-side filtering on the individual BBFrame events.

### Private / custom packet types

`PayloadRegistry` lets you register owned types for packet_type values not in
`PacketType` (or override built-in ones). Call `event.payload_with(®)` instead
of `event.payload()`; the registry's parser wins, producing `AnyPayload::Other { packet_type, value }` where `value` can be downcast to your concrete type.

## Feature flags

| Feature | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `std` | on | Link the standard library. Without it the crate is `#![no_std]`+`alloc`. |
| `ts` | on | `T2miPump`feed-and-iterate front door +`InnerTsRecovery`; pulls in`bytes`and`dvb-bbframe`. |
| `serde` | off | Serialize-only ( `serde::Serialize`) on all header and payload types; no Deserialize. |
| `chrono` | off | Decoded UTC emission-time accessor on `T2TimestampPayload`. |
| `yoke` | off | `yoke::Yokeable`on zero-copy payload view types. |

## MSRV

Rust **1.81**.

## References

- [ETSI TS 102 773 v1.4.1](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/102700_102799/102773/)— DVB-T2 Modulator Interface (T2-MI)
- [ETSI EN 302 755 v1.4.1](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/302700_302799/302755/)— DVB-T2 Frame structure, channel coding and modulation

## Examples

Run with `cargo run -p dvb-t2mi --example <name>`:

- `parse_header`
- `pump_capture`

([LICENSE-APACHE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE)), at your option.

# bytes - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bytes/^1/

## Expand description

Provides abstractions for working with bytes.

The `bytes` crate provides an efficient byte buffer structure
([ Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Bytes.html)) and traits for working with buffer
implementations (

[,](https://docs.rs/buf/trait.Buf.html)

`Buf`[).](https://docs.rs/buf/trait.BufMut.html)

`BufMut`[§](https://docs.rs#bytes)`Bytes`

`Bytes` is an efficient container for storing and operating on contiguous
slices of memory. It is intended for use primarily in networking code, but
could have applications elsewhere as well.

`Bytes` values facilitate zero-copy network programming by allowing multiple
`Bytes` objects to point to the same underlying memory. This is managed by
using a reference count to track when the memory is no longer needed and can
be freed.

A `Bytes` handle can be created directly from an existing byte store (such as `&[u8]`
or `Vec<u8>`), but usually a `BytesMut` is used first and written to. For
example:

```
use bytes::{BytesMut, BufMut};
let mut buf = BytesMut::with_capacity(1024);
buf.put(&b"hello world"[..]);
buf.put_u16(1234);
let a = buf.split();
assert_eq!(a, b"hello world\x04\xD2"[..]);
buf.put(&b"goodbye world"[..]);
let b = buf.split();
assert_eq!(b, b"goodbye world"[..]);
assert_eq!(buf.capacity(), 998);
```
In the above example, only a single buffer of 1024 is allocated. The handles
`a` and `b` will share the underlying buffer and maintain indices tracking
the view into the buffer represented by the handle.

See the [struct docs](https://docs.rs/struct.Bytes.html) for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#buf-bufmut)`Buf`, `BufMut`

These two traits provide read and write access to buffers. The underlying
storage may or may not be in contiguous memory. For example, `Bytes` is a
buffer that guarantees contiguous memory, but a [rope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rope_(data_structure)) stores the bytes in
disjoint chunks. `Buf` and `BufMut` maintain cursors tracking the current
position in the underlying byte storage. When bytes are read or written, the
cursor is advanced.

[§](https://docs.rs#relation-with-read-and-write)Relation with `Read` and `Write`

At first glance, it may seem that `Buf` and `BufMut` overlap in
functionality with [ std::io::Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html) and

[. However, they serve different purposes. A buffer is the value that is provided as an argument to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Write.html)

`std::io::Write``Read::read` and `Write::write`. `Read` and `Write` may then
perform a syscall, which has the potential of failing. Operations on `Buf`
and `BufMut` are infallible.## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buf](https://docs.rs/buf/index.html)
- Utilities for working with buffers.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Bytes.html)
- A cheaply cloneable and sliceable chunk of contiguous memory.
- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.BytesMut.html)- Mut
- A unique reference to a contiguous slice of memory.
- [TryGet](https://docs.rs/struct.TryGetError.html)- Error
- Error type for the `try_get_`methods of`Buf``Buf``try_get_`methods.

# dvb_bbframe - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-bbframe/^8/

## Expand description

ETSI DVB-S2 / S2X / T2 BBFrame parser + builder.

Supports both Normal Mode (NM) and High Efficiency Mode (HEM) per EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §5.1.7.

Entry points:

- `header::Bbheader`
- `packet::up_iter`
- `pump::BbframePump`
- `crc::crc8`
- `issy`

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, Matype, Mode, TsGs, BBHEADER_LEN};
let hdr = Bbheader {
    matype: Matype { ts_gs: TsGs::Ts, sis: true, ccm: true, issyi: false, npd: false, ext: 0, isi: 0 },
    upl: 1504, sync: 0x47, dfl: 1504, syncd: 0, mode: Mode::Normal, issy_in_header: None,
};
let bytes = hdr.serialize();              // 10-byte BBHEADER
assert_eq!(bytes.len(), BBHEADER_LEN);
assert_eq!(Bbheader::parse(&bytes).unwrap(), hdr); // byte-identical round-trip
```
For recovering the inner TS carried in a T2-MI stream, see
`dvb_t2mi::inner_ts::InnerTsRecovery`, which drives this header + the
[ packet](https://docs.rs/packet/index.html) extractor for you.

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-stream-gse-handoff)Generic Stream (GSE) handoff

When `Bbheader::parse` yields `matype.ts_gs == TsGs::Gse`, the data field
carries GSE (Generic Stream Encapsulation) packets (EN 302 307-1 / EN 302 755).
GSE parsing is out of scope for this crate — hand the data field to the
third-party `dvb-gse` crate:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, TsGs, BBHEADER_LEN};
let hdr = Bbheader::parse(df_bytes).unwrap();
let data_field = &df_bytes[BBHEADER_LEN..];
match hdr.matype.ts_gs {
    TsGs::Ts => {
        /* TS user packets: dvb_bbframe::packet::up_iter(data_field, &hdr) */
    }
    TsGs::Gse => {
        /* GSE packets: hand `data_field` to the `dvb-gse` crate */
    }
    other => {
        /* GFPS / GCS — generic continuous or packetized */
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rfu-policy)RFU policy

BBFrame `reserved_future_use` bits are **emitted as 1** and
`reserved_zero_future_use` bits as **0**, following the DVB convention.
Parsers accept any value (no rejection on non-zero RFU) for forward
compatibility.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Two runnable examples ship with this crate (`cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example <name>`).

[§](https://docs.rs#parse_bbheader)`parse_bbheader`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Basic: parse a single DVB-S2 BBHEADER from raw bytes.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example parse_bbheader`
use dvb_bbframe::crc::crc8;
use dvb_bbframe::header::Bbheader;
fn main() {
    // A 10-byte Normal-Mode BBHEADER: MATYPE-1/2, UPL, DFL, SYNC, SYNCD, CRC-8.
    // (UPL=1520 bits = a 188-byte TS packet, SYNC=0x47, TS/CCM stream.)
    #[rustfmt::skip]
    let mut header = [
        0xD8, 0x00, // MATYPE-1, MATYPE-2
        0x05, 0xF0, // UPL = 1520 bits
        0xE0, 0x30, // DFL = 57392 bits
        0x47,       // SYNC byte
        0x00, 0x00, // SYNCD
        0x00,       // CRC-8 — filled below
    ];
    // In Normal Mode the MODE field is folded into the CRC-8: a stored byte
    // equal to crc8(header[..9]) decodes back to Mode::Normal.
    header[9] = crc8(&header[..9]);
    let hdr = Bbheader::parse(&header).expect("valid BBHEADER");
    println!("mode    : {:?}", hdr.mode);
    println!("ts_gs   : {:?}", hdr.matype.ts_gs);
    println!("ccm     : {}", hdr.matype.ccm);
    println!("issyi   : {}", hdr.matype.issyi);
    println!("UPL     : {} bits", hdr.upl);
    println!("DFL     : {} bits", hdr.dfl);
    println!("SYNC    : {:#04X}", hdr.sync);
    println!("SYNCD   : {}", hdr.syncd);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#walk_capture)`walk_capture`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Advanced: walk a real DVB-S2 capture, reassemble BBFrames from TS private
//! sections, and parse every BBHEADER.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example walk_capture`
//!
//! Reads the committed `tnt-5w-12732v-bbframe.ts` fixture at runtime, so the
//! example compiles even when the fixture is absent.
use dvb_bbframe::crc::crc8;
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, Mode};
const BBFRAME_PID: u16 = 0x010E;
const NEW_FRAME_COUNT: u8 = 0xB8; // section count byte marking a new BBFrame
/// Reassemble complete BBFrames carried in TS private sections on `pid`.
fn extract_bbframes(data: &[u8], pid: u16) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    let mut current = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
    let mut started = false;
    for pkt in data.chunks(188) {
        if pkt.len() < 188 || pkt[0] != 0x47 {
            continue;
        }
        let ts_pid = ((u16::from(pkt[1]) & 0x1F) << 8) | u16::from(pkt[2]);
        if ts_pid != pid || pkt[3] & 0x30 != 0x10 {
            continue;
        }
        if pkt[4] != 0x00 || pkt[5] != 0x80 || pkt[6] != 0x00 {
            continue; // section header: 00 80 00 [slen] [count]
        }
        let slen = usize::from(pkt[7]);
        if slen == 0 || slen > 0xB4 {
            continue;
        }
        let data_end = 9 + (slen - 1);
        if data_end > 188 {
            continue;
        }
        if pkt[8] == NEW_FRAME_COUNT {
            if started && !current.is_empty() {
                frames.push(core::mem::take(&mut current));
            }
            started = true;
            current.clear();
        }
        if started {
            current.extend_from_slice(&pkt[9..data_end]);
        }
    }
    frames
}
fn main() {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/tests/fixtures/tnt-5w-12732v-bbframe.ts"
    );
    let data = match std::fs::read(path) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("fixture not available ({e}); nothing to do");
            return;
        }
    };
    let frames = extract_bbframes(&data, BBFRAME_PID);
    println!(
        "PID {BBFRAME_PID:#06X}: {} BBFrames reassembled",
        frames.len()
    );
    let mut normal = 0;
    let mut crc_ok = 0;
    for frame in &frames {
        if frame.len() < 10 {
            continue;
        }
        let hdr = Bbheader::parse(frame).expect("BBHEADER parses");
        if hdr.mode == Mode::Normal {
            normal += 1;
        }
        // NM integrity: stored CRC-8 equals computed over the first 9 bytes.
        if crc8(&frame[..9]) == frame[9] {
            crc_ok += 1;
        }
    }
    println!("Normal-Mode headers : {normal}");
    println!("CRC-8 intact        : {crc_ok}/{}", frames.len());
    if let Some(first) = frames.first() {
        let hdr = Bbheader::parse(first).unwrap();
        println!(
            "first frame         : UPL={} bits, DFL={} bits, SYNC={:#04X}",
            hdr.upl, hdr.dfl, hdr.sync
        );
    }
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [crc](https://docs.rs/crc/index.html)
- CRC-8 encoder per EN 302 755 Annex F / EN 302 307-1 §5.1.4.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error type for BBFrame parsing and serialization.
- [header](https://docs.rs/header/index.html)

# erased_serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/erased-serde/^0.4/

## Expand description

This crate provides type-erased versions of Serde’s `Serialize`, `Serializer`
and `Deserializer` traits that can be used as [trait objects](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/trait-objects.html).

The usual Serde `Serialize`, `Serializer` and `Deserializer` traits cannot
be used as trait objects like `&dyn Serialize` or boxed trait objects like
`Box<dyn Serialize>` because of Rust’s [“object safety” rules](http://huonw.github.io/blog/2015/01/object-safety/). In
particular, all three traits contain generic methods which cannot be made
into a trait object.

This library should be considered a low-level building block for interacting
with Serde APIs in an object-safe way. Most use cases will require higher
level functionality such as provided by [ typetag](https://github.com/dtolnay/typetag) which uses this crate
internally.

**The traits in this crate work seamlessly with any existing Serde
 Serialize and Deserialize type and any existing Serde Serializer and
Deserializer format.**

[§](https://docs.rs#serialization)Serialization

```
use erased_serde::{Serialize, Serializer};
use std::collections::BTreeMap as Map;
use std::io;
fn main() {
    // Construct some serializers.
    let json = &mut serde_json::Serializer::new(io::stdout());
    let cbor = &mut serde_cbor::Serializer::new(serde_cbor::ser::IoWrite::new(io::stdout()));
    // The values in this map are boxed trait objects. Ordinarily this would not
    // be possible with serde::Serializer because of object safety, but type
    // erasure makes it possible with erased_serde::Serializer.
    let mut formats: Map<&str, Box<dyn Serializer>> = Map::new();
    formats.insert("json", Box::new(<dyn Serializer>::erase(json)));
    formats.insert("cbor", Box::new(<dyn Serializer>::erase(cbor)));
    // These are boxed trait objects as well. Same thing here - type erasure
    // makes this possible.
    let mut values: Map<&str, Box<dyn Serialize>> = Map::new();
    values.insert("vec", Box::new(vec!["a", "b"]));
    values.insert("int", Box::new(65536));
    // Pick a Serializer out of the formats map.
    let format = formats.get_mut("json").unwrap();
    // Pick a Serialize out of the values map.
    let value = values.get("vec").unwrap();
    // This line prints `["a","b"]` to stdout.
    value.erased_serialize(format).unwrap();
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#deserialization)Deserialization

```
use erased_serde::Deserializer;
use std::collections::BTreeMap as Map;
fn main() {
    static JSON: &'static [u8] = br#"{"A": 65, "B": 66}"#;
    static CBOR: &'static [u8] = &[162, 97, 65, 24, 65, 97, 66, 24, 66];
    // Construct some deserializers.
    let json = &mut serde_json::Deserializer::from_slice(JSON);
    let cbor = &mut serde_cbor::Deserializer::from_slice(CBOR);
    // The values in this map are boxed trait objects, which is not possible
    // with the normal serde::Deserializer because of object safety.
    let mut formats: Map<&str, Box<dyn Deserializer>> = Map::new();
    formats.insert("json", Box::new(<dyn Deserializer>::erase(json)));
    formats.insert("cbor", Box::new(<dyn Deserializer>::erase(cbor)));
    // Pick a Deserializer out of the formats map.
    let format = formats.get_mut("json").unwrap();
    let data: Map<String, usize> = erased_serde::deserialize(format).unwrap();
    println!("{}", data["A"] + data["B"]);
}
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [serialize_](https://docs.rs/macro.serialize_trait_object.html)- trait_ - object
- Implement `serde::Serialize`for a trait object that has`erased_serde::Serialize`as a supertrait.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- Error when a `Serializer`or`Deserializer`trait object fails.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- An object-safe equivalent of Serde’s `Deserializer`trait.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- An object-safe equivalent of Serde’s `Serialize`trait.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- An object-safe equivalent of Serde’s `Serializer`trait.

- Deserialize a value of type `T`from the given trait object.
- [serialize](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize.html)
- Serialize the given type-erased serializable value.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Result type alias where the error is `erased_serde::Error`.
