# num_enum - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/num_enum/^0.7/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#num_enum)num_enum

Procedural macros to make inter-operation between primitives and enums easier. This crate is no_std compatible.

[§](https://docs.rs#turning-an-enum-into-a-primitive)Turning an enum into a primitive

```
use num_enum::IntoPrimitive;
#[derive(IntoPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero,
    One,
}
fn main() {
    let zero: u8 = Number::Zero.into();
    assert_eq!(zero, 0u8);
}
```
`num_enum`’s `IntoPrimitive` is more type-safe than using `as`, because `as` will silently truncate - `num_enum` only derives `From` for exactly the discriminant type of the enum.

[§](https://docs.rs#attempting-to-turn-a-primitive-into-an-enum-with-try_from)Attempting to turn a primitive into an enum with try_from

```
use num_enum::TryFromPrimitive;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, TryFromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero,
    One,
}
fn main() {
    let zero = Number::try_from(0u8);
    assert_eq!(zero, Ok(Number::Zero));
    let three = Number::try_from(3u8);
    assert_eq!(
        three.unwrap_err().to_string(),
        "No discriminant in enum `Number` matches the value `3`",
    );
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant-alternatives)Variant alternatives

Sometimes a single enum variant might be representable by multiple numeric values.

The `#[num_enum(alternatives = [..])]` attribute allows you to define additional value alternatives for individual variants.

(The behavior of `IntoPrimitive` is unaffected by this attribute, it will always return the canonical value.)

```
use num_enum::TryFromPrimitive;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, TryFromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero = 0,
    #[num_enum(alternatives = [2])]
    OneOrTwo = 1,
}
fn main() {
    let zero = Number::try_from(0u8);
    assert_eq!(zero, Ok(Number::Zero));
    let one = Number::try_from(1u8);
    assert_eq!(one, Ok(Number::OneOrTwo));
    let two = Number::try_from(2u8);
    assert_eq!(two, Ok(Number::OneOrTwo));
    let three = Number::try_from(3u8);
    assert_eq!(
        three.unwrap_err().to_string(),
        "No discriminant in enum `Number` matches the value `3`",
    );
}
```
Range expressions are also supported for alternatives, but this requires enabling the `complex-expressions` feature:

```
use num_enum::TryFromPrimitive;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, TryFromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero = 0,
    #[num_enum(alternatives = [2..16])]
    Some = 1,
    #[num_enum(alternatives = [17, 18..=255])]
    Many = 16,
}
fn main() {
    let zero = Number::try_from(0u8);
    assert_eq!(zero, Ok(Number::Zero));
    let some = Number::try_from(15u8);
    assert_eq!(some, Ok(Number::Some));
    let many = Number::try_from(255u8);
    assert_eq!(many, Ok(Number::Many));
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-error-types)Custom error types

`TryFromPrimitive` by default will use `num_enum::TryFromPrimitiveError` as its `Error` type.

If you want to use a different type, you can use an annotation for this:

```
use num_enum::TryFromPrimitive;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, TryFromPrimitive)]
#[num_enum(error_type(name = CustomError, constructor = CustomError::new))]
#[repr(u8)]
enum FirstNumber {
    Zero,
    One,
    Two,
}
struct CustomError {}
impl CustomError {
    fn new(value: u8) -> CustomError {
        CustomError {}
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#safely-turning-a-primitive-into-an-exhaustive-enum-with-from_primitive)Safely turning a primitive into an exhaustive enum with from_primitive

If your enum has all possible primitive values covered, you can derive `FromPrimitive` for it (which auto-implement stdlib’s `From`):

You can cover all possible values by:

- Having variants for every possible value
- Having a variant marked `#[num_enum(default)]`
- Having a variant marked `#[num_enum(catch_all)]`
- Having `#[num_enum(alternatives = [...])`s covering values not covered by a variant.

```
use num_enum::FromPrimitive;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, FromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero,
    #[num_enum(default)]
    NonZero,
}
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        Number::Zero,
        Number::from(0_u8),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        Number::NonZero,
        Number::from(1_u8),
    );
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-variant)Default variant

Sometimes it is desirable to have an `Other` variant in an enum that acts as a kind of a wildcard matching all the value not yet covered by other variants.

The `#[num_enum(default)]` attribute (or the stdlib `#[default]` attribute) allows you to mark variant as the default.

(The behavior of `IntoPrimitive` is unaffected by this attribute, it will always return the canonical value.)

```
use num_enum::FromPrimitive;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, FromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero = 0,
    #[num_enum(default)]
    NonZero = 1,
}
fn main() {
    let zero = Number::from(0u8);
    assert_eq!(zero, Number::Zero);
    let one = Number::from(1u8);
    assert_eq!(one, Number::NonZero);
    let two = Number::from(2u8);
    assert_eq!(two, Number::NonZero);
}
```
Only `FromPrimitive` pays attention to `default` attributes, `TryFromPrimitive` ignores them.

[§](https://docs.rs#catch-all-variant)Catch-all variant

Sometimes it is desirable to have an `Other` variant which holds the otherwise un-matched value as a field.

The `#[num_enum(catch_all)]` attribute allows you to mark at most one variant for this purpose. The variant it’s applied to must be a tuple variant with exactly one field matching the `repr` type.

```
use num_enum::FromPrimitive;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, FromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero = 0,
    #[num_enum(catch_all)]
    NonZero(u8),
}
fn main() {
    let zero = Number::from(0u8);
    assert_eq!(zero, Number::Zero);
    let one = Number::from(1u8);
    assert_eq!(one, Number::NonZero(1_u8));
    let two = Number::from(2u8);
    assert_eq!(two, Number::NonZero(2_u8));
}
```
As this is naturally exhaustive, this is only supported for `FromPrimitive`, not also `TryFromPrimitive`.

[§](https://docs.rs#unsafely-turning-a-primitive-into-an-enum-with-unchecked_transmute_from)Unsafely turning a primitive into an enum with unchecked_transmute_from

If you’re really certain a conversion will succeed (and have not made use of `#[num_enum(default)]` or `#[num_enum(alternatives = [..])]`
for any of its variants), and want to avoid a small amount of overhead, you can use unsafe code to do this conversion.
Unless you have data showing that the match statement generated in the `try_from` above is a bottleneck for you,
you should avoid doing this, as the unsafe code has potential to cause serious memory issues in your program.

```
use num_enum::UnsafeFromPrimitive;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, UnsafeFromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero,
    One,
}
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(
        unsafe { Number::unchecked_transmute_from(0_u8) },
        Number::Zero,
    );
    assert_eq!(
        unsafe { Number::unchecked_transmute_from(1_u8) },
        Number::One,
    );
}
unsafe fn undefined_behavior() {
    let _ = Number::unchecked_transmute_from(2); // 2 is not a valid discriminant!
}
```
Note that this derive ignores any `default`, `catch_all`, and `alternatives` attributes on the enum.
If you need support for conversions from these values, you should use `TryFromPrimitive` or `FromPrimitive`.

This means, for instance, that the following is undefined behaviour:

```
use num_enum::UnsafeFromPrimitive;
#[derive(UnsafeFromPrimitive)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum Number {
    Zero = 0,
    // Same for `#[num_enum(catch_all)]`, and `#[num_enum(alternatives = [2, ...])]`
    #[num_enum(default)]
    One = 1,
}
let _undefined_behavior = unsafe { Number::unchecked_transmute_from(2) };
```
[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

Some enum values may be composed of complex expressions, for example:

```
enum Number {
    Zero = (0, 1).0,
    One = (0, 1).1,
}
```
To cut down on compile time, these are not supported by default, but if you enable the `complex-expressions`
feature of your dependency on `num_enum`, these should start working.

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

num_enum may be used under your choice of the BSD 3-clause, Apache 2, or MIT license.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Default](https://docs.rs/derive.Default.html)
- Implements `core::default::Default`for a`#[repr(Primitive)] enum`.
- [From](https://docs.rs/derive.FromPrimitive.html)- Primitive
- Implements `From<Primitive>`for a`#[repr(Primitive)] enum`.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/derive.IntoPrimitive.html)- Primitive
- Implements `Into<Primitive>`for a`#[repr(Primitive)] enum`.
- [TryFrom](https://docs.rs/derive.TryFromPrimitive.html)- Primitive
- Implements `TryFrom<Primitive>`for a`#[repr(Primitive)] enum`.

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/^2/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

# yoke - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yoke/^0.7/

## Expand description

This crate provides [ Yoke<Y, C>](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html), which allows one to “yoke” (attach) a zero-copy deserialized
object (say, a

[) to the source it was deserialized from, (say, an](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html)

`Cow<'a, str>`[), known in this crate as a “cart”, producing a type that looks like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/rc/struct.Rc.html)

`Rc<[u8]>``Yoke<Cow<'static, str>, Rc<[u8]>>`
and can be moved around with impunity.Succinctly, this allows one to “erase” static lifetimes and turn them into dynamic ones, similarly
to how `dyn` allows one to “erase” static types and turn them into dynamic ones.

Most of the time the yokeable `Y` type will be some kind of zero-copy deserializable
abstraction, potentially with an owned variant (like [ Cow](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/borrow/enum.Cow.html),

[, or an aggregate containing such types), and the cart](https://docs.rs/zerovec)

`ZeroVec``C` will be some smart pointer like
[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<T>`[, or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/rc/struct.Rc.html)

`Rc<T>`[, potentially wrapped in an](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)

`Arc<T>`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)

`Option<T>`The key behind this crate is [ Yoke::get()](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html#method.get), where calling

[on a type like](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html#method.get)

`.get()``Yoke<Cow<'static, str>, _>` will get you a short-lived `&'a Cow<'a, str>`, restricted to the
lifetime of the borrow used during [. This is entirely safe since the](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html#method.get)

`.get()``Cow` borrows from
the cart type `C`, which cannot be interfered with as long as the `Yoke` is borrowed by [.](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html#method.get)

`.get()`[protects access by essentially reifying the erased lifetime to a safe local one when necessary.](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html#method.get)

`.get()`See the documentation of [ Yoke](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html) for more details.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [cartable_](https://docs.rs/cartable_ptr/index.html)- ptr
- Types for optional pointers with niche optimization.
- [either](https://docs.rs/either/index.html)
- Types to enable polymorphic carts.
- [erased](https://docs.rs/erased/index.html)
- This module contains helper types for erasing Cart types.
- [trait_](https://docs.rs/trait_hack/index.html)- hack
- Workarounds for adding trait bounds to `yoke`objects.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Yoke](https://docs.rs/struct.Yoke.html)
- A Cow-like borrowed object “yoked” to its backing data.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Cloneable](https://docs.rs/trait.CloneableCart.html)- Cart
- This trait marks cart types that do not change source on cloning
- [Yokeable](https://docs.rs/trait.Yokeable.html)
- The `Yokeable<'a>`trait is implemented on the`'static`version of any zero-copy type; for example,`Cow<'static, T>`implements`Yokeable<'a>`(for all`'a`).

- [Yokeable](https://docs.rs/derive.Yokeable.html)
- Custom derive for `yoke::Yokeable`,

# criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.5/

## Expand description

A statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library written in Rust.

This crate is a microbenchmarking library which aims to provide strong statistical confidence in detecting and estimating the size of performance improvements and regressions, while also being easy to use.

See
[the user guide](https://bheisler.github.io/criterion.rs/book/index.html)
for examples as well as details on the measurement and analysis process,
and the output.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Collects detailed statistics, providing strong confidence that changes to performance are real, not measurement noise.
- Produces detailed charts, providing thorough understanding of your code’s performance behavior.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_executor/index.html)- executor
- This module defines a trait that can be used to plug in different Futures executors into Criterion.rs’ async benchmarking support.
- [measurement](https://docs.rs/measurement/index.html)
- This module defines a set of traits that can be used to plug different measurements (eg.
Unix’s Processor Time, CPU or GPU performance counters, etc.) into Criterion.rs. It also
includes the [WallTime](https://docs.rs/struct.WallTime.html)struct which defines the default wall-clock time measurement.
- [profiler](https://docs.rs/profiler/index.html)
- This module provides an extension trait which allows in-process profilers
to be hooked into the `--profile-time`argument at compile-time. Users of out-of-process profilers such as perf don’t need to do anything special.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_group.html)- group
- Macro used to define a function group for the benchmark harness; see the
`criterion_main!`macro for more details.
- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_main.html)- main
- Macro which expands to a benchmark harness.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncBencher.html)- Bencher
- Async/await variant of the Bencher struct.
- [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)
- Timer struct used to iterate a benchmarked function and measure the runtime.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)- Group
- Structure used to group together a set of related benchmarks, along with custom configuration settings for groups of benchmarks. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkId.html)- Id
- Simple structure representing an ID for a benchmark. The ID must be unique within a benchmark group.
- [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)
- The benchmark manager
- [Plot](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Axis](https://docs.rs/enum.AxisScale.html)- Scale
- Axis scaling type
- [Baseline](https://docs.rs/enum.Baseline.html)
- Baseline describes how the baseline_directory is handled.
- [Batch](https://docs.rs/enum.BatchSize.html)- Size
- Argument to `Bencher::iter_batched``Bencher::iter_batched_ref`
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/enum.BenchmarkFilter.html)- Filter
- Benchmark filtering support.
- [Plotting](https://docs.rs/enum.PlottingBackend.html)- Backend
- Enum used to select the plotting backend.
- [Sampling](https://docs.rs/enum.SamplingMode.html)- Mode
- This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling. The default is Auto, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.
- [Throughput](https://docs.rs/enum.Throughput.html)
- Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [black_](https://docs.rs/fn.black_box.html)- box
- A function that is opaque to the optimizer, used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away computations in a benchmark.

---

# dvb_t2mi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/target-redirect/dvb_t2mi/

## Expand description

ETSI TS 102 773 v1.4.1 DVB-T2 Modulator Interface (T2-MI) parser + builder.

Entry points:

- `Parse`- `Serialize`
- `packet`
- `payload`
- `payload::PayloadRegistry`- `pump::T2miEvent::payload_with`
- `payload::AnyPayload::dispatch_with`
- `crc`

[§](https://docs.rs#rfu-policy)RFU policy

Payload parsers REJECT non-zero reserved (rfu) bits with
`ReservedBitsViolation` and serialize them as 0 — with one deliberate
exception: individual addressing (0x21) PRESERVES its leading rfu byte
verbatim so gateway streams round-trip byte-exact (see
`payload::individual_addressing`).

[§](https://docs.rs#quickstart-pump-a-ts-get-typed-payloads)Quickstart: pump a TS, get typed payloads

[ pump::T2miPump](https://docs.rs/pump/struct.T2miPump.html) filters a TS by PID, reassembles + CRC-validates T2-MI
packets, and hands back events whose

[dispatches to a typed](https://docs.rs/pump/struct.T2miEvent.html#method.payload)

`payload`[:](https://docs.rs/payload/any/enum.AnyPayload.html)

`payload::AnyPayload````
use dvb_t2mi::pump::T2miPump;
use dvb_t2mi::payload::AnyPayload;
let mut pump = T2miPump::new(0x0006); // T2-MI PID from the PMT
for packet in &ts_packets {          // each aligned 188-byte TS packet
    for event in pump.feed_ts(packet) {
        if let Ok(AnyPayload::Bbframe(bb)) = event.payload() {
            println!("BBFrame plp_id={}", bb.plp_id);
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#the-full-signal-chain)The full signal chain

T2-MI carries DVB-T2 BBFrames, which carry the inner MPEG-TS, which carries
SI. The crates compose end to end — T2-MI here, BBFrame extraction in
[ dvb-bbframe](https://docs.rs/dvb-bbframe), SI demux in

[:](https://docs.rs/dvb-si)

`dvb-si````
TS (T2-MI PID) ─▶ T2miPump ─▶ AnyPayload::Bbframe
                                  │ bb.bbframe
                                  ▼
                         dvb_bbframe::Bbheader::parse + up_iter
                                  │ inner TS packets
                                  ▼
                         dvb_si::demux::SiDemux ─▶ AnyTableSection
```
A complete, working version of this chain (synthetic fixture, every layer
built and asserted) lives in `dvb-t2mi/tests/chain.rs`.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

| Feature | Default | Enables |
|---|---|---|
| `ts` | on | — PID-filtered TS reassembly + CRC validation. Off → bring your own complete T2-MI packet bytes.`pump::T2miPump` |
| `serde` | on | Serialize-only— for display/export (JSON via serde_json); parsing FROM JSON is deliberately unsupported, re-parse from wire bytes.`Serialize`on every packet/payload type. |
| `yoke` | off | on the zero-copy payload view types — own a parsed T2-MI payload past the input buffer’s borrow without re-parsing.`yoke::Yokeable` |

[§](https://docs.rs#header-only-example)Header-only example

```
use dvb_t2mi::packet::Header;
use broadcast_common::Parse;
let buf = [0x00u8, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00];
let hdr = Header::parse(&buf[..]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(hdr.payload_len_bits, 0);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Two runnable examples ship with this crate (`cargo run -p dvb-t2mi --example <name>`).

[§](https://docs.rs#parse_header)`parse_header`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Basic: parse a T2-MI packet header from raw bytes.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-t2mi --example parse_header`
use broadcast_common::Parse;
use dvb_t2mi::packet::Header;
fn main() {
    // A 6-byte T2-MI packet header: packet_type, packet_count, superframe_idx,
    // reserved, and a 16-bit payload length in bits (here: 0).
    let bytes = [0x00u8, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00];
    let hdr = Header::parse(&bytes).expect("valid T2-MI header");
    println!("packet_type     : {:?}", hdr.packet_type);
    println!("packet_count    : {}", hdr.packet_count);
    println!("superframe_idx  : {}", hdr.superframe_idx);
    println!("payload_len_bits: {}", hdr.payload_len_bits);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#pump_capture)`pump_capture`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Advanced: pump a real T2-MI stream out of an MPEG-TS capture and tally the
//! payload types (BBFrames, L1 signalling, timestamps).
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-t2mi --example pump_capture` (needs the default
//! `ts` feature). Reads the committed `colombia-capital-t2mi.ts` fixture at
//! runtime.
use dvb_t2mi::payload::AnyPayload;
use dvb_t2mi::pump::T2miPump;
const T2MI_PID: u16 = 0x0040;
const PKT: usize = 188;
fn main() {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/tests/fixtures/colombia-capital-t2mi.ts"
    );
    let data = match std::fs::read(path) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("fixture not available ({e}); nothing to do");
            return;
        }
    };
    let mut pump = T2miPump::new(T2MI_PID);
    let (mut bbframes, mut l1, mut timestamps, mut other) = (0u32, 0u32, 0u32, 0u32);
    for pkt in data.chunks(PKT) {
        if pkt.len() < PKT {
            break;
        }
        for event in pump.feed_ts(pkt) {
            match event.payload() {
                Ok(AnyPayload::Bbframe(_)) => bbframes += 1,
                Ok(AnyPayload::L1Current(_)) => l1 += 1,
                Ok(AnyPayload::Timestamp(_)) => timestamps += 1,
                Ok(_) => other += 1,
                Err(_) => {}
            }
        }
    }
    println!("T2-MI on PID {T2MI_PID:#06X}:");
    println!("  BBFrame payloads   : {bbframes}");
    println!("  L1-current packets : {l1}");
    println!("  timestamp packets  : {timestamps}");
    println!("  other payloads     : {other}");
    println!("  CRC-32 failures    : {}", pump.stats().crc_failures);
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [crc](https://docs.rs/crc/index.html)
- T2-MI CRC helpers.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error type returned by every parser in this crate.
- [inner_](https://docs.rs/inner_ts/index.html)- ts - `ts`
- Inner-TS recovery — the single driver from a T2-MI PID to the inner MPEG-TS.
- [packet](https://docs.rs/packet/index.html)
- T2-MI packet header and type parsing.
- [payload](https://docs.rs/payload/index.html)
- T2-MI payload types (§5.2.1 - §5.2.12).
- [pump](https://docs.rs/pump/index.html)- `ts`
- `T2miPump`- `Bytes`
- [traits](https://docs.rs/traits/index.html)
- T2-MI–specific traits. `Parse`/`Serialize`are provided by`broadcast_common`and imported directly at call sites.
- [ts](https://docs.rs/ts/index.html)- `ts`
- TS packet reassembly utilities.

//! Advanced: pump a real T2-MI stream out of an MPEG-TS capture and tally the
//! payload types (BBFrames, L1 signalling, timestamps).

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/src/dvb_t2mi/lib.rs.html

# dvb_t2mi/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! ETSI TS 102 773 v1.4.1 DVB-T2 Modulator Interface (T2-MI) parser + builder.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Entry points:
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! - [`Parse`](broadcast_common::Parse) / [`Serialize`](broadcast_common::Serialize) — the two
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!   symmetric contracts every payload type implements.
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! - [`packet`] — T2-MI packet header and type parsing.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! - [`payload`] — BBFrame, L1, FEF, timestamp, and addressing payload types.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! - [`payload::PayloadRegistry`] / [`pump::T2miEvent::payload_with`] — register
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!   private packet types and dispatch through the registry.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! - [`payload::AnyPayload::dispatch_with`] — registry-aware dispatch for custom types.
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! - [`crc`] — CRC-32 per Annex A.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! # RFU policy
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! Payload parsers REJECT non-zero reserved (rfu) bits with
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! `ReservedBitsViolation` and serialize them as 0 — with one deliberate
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! exception: individual addressing (0x21) PRESERVES its leading rfu byte
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! verbatim so gateway streams round-trip byte-exact (see
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! `payload::individual_addressing`).
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! # Quickstart: pump a TS, get typed payloads
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! [`pump::T2miPump`] filters a TS by PID, reassembles + CRC-validates T2-MI
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! packets, and hands back events whose [`payload`](pump::T2miEvent::payload)
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! dispatches to a typed [`payload::AnyPayload`]:
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ```no_run
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! # #[cfg(feature = "ts")] {
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! use dvb_t2mi::pump::T2miPump;
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! use dvb_t2mi::payload::AnyPayload;
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! let mut pump = T2miPump::new(0x0006); // T2-MI PID from the PMT
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! # let ts_packets: Vec<[u8; 188]> = Vec::new();
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! for packet in &ts_packets {          // each aligned 188-byte TS packet
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!     for event in pump.feed_ts(packet) {
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!         if let Ok(AnyPayload::Bbframe(bb)) = event.payload() {
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!             println!("BBFrame plp_id={}", bb.plp_id);
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//!         }
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!     }
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! }
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! # }
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! ```
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! # The full signal chain
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! T2-MI carries DVB-T2 BBFrames, which carry the inner MPEG-TS, which carries
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! SI. The crates compose end to end — T2-MI here, BBFrame extraction in
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! [`dvb-bbframe`](https://docs.rs/dvb-bbframe), SI demux in
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! [`dvb-si`](https://docs.rs/dvb-si):
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! ```text
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! TS (T2-MI PID) ─▶ T2miPump ─▶ AnyPayload::Bbframe
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!                                   │ bb.bbframe
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!                                   ▼
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!                          dvb_bbframe::Bbheader::parse + up_iter
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!                                   │ inner TS packets
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!                                   ▼
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//!                          dvb_si::demux::SiDemux ─▶ AnyTableSection
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! ```
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! A complete, working version of this chain (synthetic fixture, every layer
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! built and asserted) lives in `dvb-t2mi/tests/chain.rs`.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! # Features
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! | Feature | Default | Enables |
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! |---|---|---|
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! | `ts` | on | [`pump::T2miPump`] — PID-filtered TS reassembly + CRC validation. Off → bring your own complete T2-MI packet bytes. |
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! | `serde` | on | **Serialize-only** — for display/export (JSON via serde_json); parsing FROM JSON is deliberately unsupported, re-parse from wire bytes. `Serialize` on every packet/payload type. |
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! | `yoke` | off | [`yoke::Yokeable`] on the zero-copy payload view types — own a parsed T2-MI payload past the input buffer's borrow without re-parsing. |
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! # Header-only example
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! ```
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! use dvb_t2mi::packet::Header;
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! use broadcast_common::Parse;
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! let buf = [0x00u8, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00];
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! let hdr = Header::parse(&buf[..]).unwrap();
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! assert_eq!(hdr.payload_len_bits, 0);
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! ```
[81](https://docs.rs#81)
[82](https://docs.rs#82)#![warn(missing_docs)]
[83](https://docs.rs#83)#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]

# Parse in broadcast_common::traits - Rust

`pub trait Parse<'a>: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    type [Error](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Error);
    // Required method
    fn [parse](https://docs.rs#tymethod.parse)(bytes: &'a [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, Self::[Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Parse.html#associatedtype.Error)>;
}## Expand description

Parse a DVB structure from raw bytes. Borrowing allowed via `<'a>`; the
concrete error type is chosen per implementer.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

pub trait Serialize {
    type
```
[Error](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.Error);
    // Required methods
    fn [serialized_len](https://docs.rs#tymethod.serialized_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html);
[serialize_into](https://docs.rs#tymethod.serialize_into)(&self, buf: &mut [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), Self::[Error](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html#associatedtype.Error)>;
    // Provided method
    fn [to_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.to_bytes)(&self) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

}## Expand description

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Convenience: allocate a `Vec` and serialise into it.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if `serialize_into` returns an error on a buffer of exactly
`serialized_len()` bytes. For values obtained by parsing real wire data
this never happens; it can only occur for a **hand-constructed** value
that violates a wire constraint (e.g. a section whose body exceeds the
12-bit `section_length`). When building values by hand and that’s a
possibility, call [ serialize_into](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html#tymethod.serialize_into) and handle the
error instead.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# PayloadRegistry in dvb_t2mi::payload::registry - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/dvb_t2mi/payload/registry/struct.PayloadRegistry.html

`pub struct PayloadRegistry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Runtime-configurable payload registry.

By default the registry has no custom parsers.  Use
[ register](https://docs.rs/struct.PayloadRegistry.html#method.register) to add private types, then call

[to dispatch through the registry.](https://docs.rs/any/enum.AnyPayload.html#method.dispatch_with)

`crate::payload::AnyPayload::dispatch_with`[§](https://docs.rs#precedence-per-entry)Precedence (per entry)

- Custom-registered parser (packet_type in the `register``crate::payload::AnyPayload::Other`
- Built-in dispatch (internal `crate::payload::AnyPayload::dispatch`
- Unknown → `crate::payload::AnyPayload::Unknown`

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Register an owned custom payload type for its
[ PayloadDef::PACKET_TYPE](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.PayloadDef.html#associatedconstant.PACKET_TYPE).

[§](https://docs.rs#owned-types-only)Owned types only

`T` must be `'static` — no borrowed slices.  The registered value is
type-erased as `Box<dyn PayloadObject>`; `dyn Any` downcast requires
the concrete type to be `'static`.

Registering a type whose `PACKET_TYPE` is already used by a built-in
**overrides** the built-in for that packet_type (custom wins precedence
in [ crate::payload::AnyPayload::dispatch_with](https://docs.rs/any/enum.AnyPayload.html#method.dispatch_with)).

Re-registering the same packet_type replaces the prior custom parser
(last wins).  A failing custom parse surfaces the client’s
`Parse::Error` unwrapped — embed identifying context (type/ packet_type)
in your error’s `what`/`reason` fields.

# T2miEvent in dvb_t2mi::pump - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/dvb_t2mi/pump/struct.T2miEvent.html

`pub struct T2miEvent { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`ts`## Expand description

One complete, CRC-valid T2-MI packet. Owns its bytes — `'static`, cheap clone.

Only constructed after CRC-32 validation (ETSI TS 102 773 Annex A).
[ T2miEvent::header](https://docs.rs/struct.T2miEvent.html#method.header) and

[are lazy: they borrow from the owned](https://docs.rs/struct.T2miEvent.html#method.payload)

`T2miEvent::payload`[on demand.](https://docs.rs/bytes/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bytes/bytes/struct.Bytes.html)

#### pub fn [packet_type](https://docs.rs#method.packet_type)(&self) -> [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)

The raw `packet_type` byte (byte 0 of the T2-MI header per §5.1).

Never panics — events are only built for CRC-valid packets which are at
least `6` (header) + `4` (CRC) = 10 bytes.

}## Expand description

Every crate-implemented T2-MI payload, plus an `Unknown` fallthrough.

serde uses external tagging with camelCase variant keys. Variant names map 1:1 to the payload modules; see each module for the wire layout.

[§](https://docs.rs#dispatch-contract)Dispatch contract

Use [ AnyPayload::dispatch](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyPayload.html#method.dispatch) with the payload bytes (post-header,
pre-CRC). See the module-level documentation for details.

### impl<'a> [AnyPayload](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyPayload.html)<'a>

Parse one payload by its `packet_type`.

`payload_bytes` must be the **payload-only slice** (bytes after
the 6-byte T2-MI header, before the 4-byte CRC trailer).

Returns `None` when `packet_type` has no typed implementation
(the caller turns that into [ AnyPayload::Unknown](https://docs.rs/enum.AnyPayload.html#variant.Unknown)).
Returns

`Some(Err)` on a typed parse failure for a recognised type.See the [module-level documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html) for the dispatch
contract (payload-only bytes, header and CRC excluded).

#### pub fn [dispatch_with](https://docs.rs#method.dispatch_with)(
    registry: &[PayloadRegistry](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.PayloadRegistry.html),
    packet_type: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html),
    payload_bytes: &'a [[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Result](https://docs.rs/error/type.Result.html)<Self>>

Parse one payload by its `packet_type`, preferring the registry’s custom
parsers over the built-in dispatch.

`payload_bytes` must be the **payload-only slice** (bytes after the
6-byte T2-MI header, before the 4-byte CRC trailer).

[§](https://docs.rs#precedence)Precedence

- If `registry`holds a custom parser for`packet_type`, it is called; the result becomes`AnyPayload::Other`
- Otherwise, falls back to the built-in `AnyPayload::dispatch`
- If neither route handles `packet_type`, returns`None`— the caller turns that into`AnyPayload::Unknown`

See the [module-level documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html) for the dispatch contract
(payload-only bytes, header and CRC excluded).

# dvb_t2mi::crc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/dvb_t2mi/crc/index.html

## Expand description

T2-MI CRC helpers.

The CRC-32 MPEG-2 primitive lives in `broadcast_common::crc32_mpeg2`.
This module keeps the T2-MI-packet-level validator, whose trailer
position semantics come from TS 102 773 §5.1 — a T2-MI-framing
concern, not a CRC primitive.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [CRC_LEN](https://docs.rs/constant.CRC_LEN.html)
- Length of the CRC-32 trailer in each T2-MI packet.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_crc.html)- crc
- Validate a T2-MI packet’s 4-byte CRC-32 trailer.

# T2miPump in dvb_t2mi::pump - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-t2mi/8.2.1/dvb_t2mi/pump/struct.T2miPump.html

`pub struct T2miPump { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`ts`## Expand description

Feed-and-iterate T2-MI pump.

Supports two operating modes:

-
**TS-encapsulated**(most common): construct with`T2miPump::new``T2miPump::feed_ts``PacketReassembler`
-
**Raw**(un-encapsulated): construct with`T2miPump::raw``T2miPump::feed_raw``payload_len_bits`) is available.

[§](https://docs.rs#pid-note)PID note

PIDs are 13-bit values (0x0000–0x1FFF per ISO/IEC 13818-1 §2.4.3.2).
This type uses `u16` directly; no newtype is introduced.  Values above
0x1FFF are accepted without error — the PID filter simply never matches.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a TS-encapsulated pump that filters to `pid`.

`pid` is the 13-bit T2-MI PID from the PMT (e.g. 0x0006 for data
piping).

[§](https://docs.rs#pid-range)PID range

Valid MPEG-TS PIDs are 13-bit (0x0000–0x1FFF); this parameter is `u16`.
No newtype is introduced to keep the API lightweight.

Create an un-encapsulated raw-stream pump.

Use [ T2miPump::feed_raw](https://docs.rs/struct.T2miPump.html#method.feed_raw) to supply bytes.  The pump buffers internally
and emits events by packet boundary, not by call boundary — a packet
split across two

`feed_raw` calls produces exactly one event.Feed one 188-byte MPEG-TS packet. Infallible: malformed packets are
counted in [ Stats::malformed_packets](https://docs.rs/struct.Stats.html#structfield.malformed_packets) and discarded.

Packets on the wrong PID are silently ignored (only [ Stats::ts_packets](https://docs.rs/struct.Stats.html#structfield.ts_packets)
is incremented).

Returns a draining iterator over any T2-MI events completed by this feed.

Feed raw T2-MI bytes (un-encapsulated mode).

The slice may contain a partial packet; bytes are buffered internally.
A packet split across two `feed_raw` calls produces exactly one event.

Returns a draining iterator over any T2-MI events completed by this feed.

# dvb_bbframe - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dvb-bbframe

## Expand description

ETSI DVB-S2 / S2X / T2 BBFrame parser + builder.

Supports both Normal Mode (NM) and High Efficiency Mode (HEM) per EN 302 755 v1.4.1 §5.1.7.

Entry points:

- `header::Bbheader`
- `packet::up_iter`
- `pump::BbframePump`
- `crc::crc8`
- `issy`

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-start)Quick start

```
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, Matype, Mode, TsGs, BBHEADER_LEN};
let hdr = Bbheader {
    matype: Matype { ts_gs: TsGs::Ts, sis: true, ccm: true, issyi: false, npd: false, ext: 0, isi: 0 },
    upl: 1504, sync: 0x47, dfl: 1504, syncd: 0, mode: Mode::Normal, issy_in_header: None,
};
let bytes = hdr.serialize();              // 10-byte BBHEADER
assert_eq!(bytes.len(), BBHEADER_LEN);
assert_eq!(Bbheader::parse(&bytes).unwrap(), hdr); // byte-identical round-trip
```
For recovering the inner TS carried in a T2-MI stream, see
`dvb_t2mi::inner_ts::InnerTsRecovery`, which drives this header + the
[ packet](https://docs.rs/packet/index.html) extractor for you.

[§](https://docs.rs#generic-stream-gse-handoff)Generic Stream (GSE) handoff

When `Bbheader::parse` yields `matype.ts_gs == TsGs::Gse`, the data field
carries GSE (Generic Stream Encapsulation) packets (EN 302 307-1 / EN 302 755).
GSE parsing is out of scope for this crate — hand the data field to the
third-party `dvb-gse` crate:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, TsGs, BBHEADER_LEN};
let hdr = Bbheader::parse(df_bytes).unwrap();
let data_field = &df_bytes[BBHEADER_LEN..];
match hdr.matype.ts_gs {
    TsGs::Ts => {
        /* TS user packets: dvb_bbframe::packet::up_iter(data_field, &hdr) */
    }
    TsGs::Gse => {
        /* GSE packets: hand `data_field` to the `dvb-gse` crate */
    }
    other => {
        /* GFPS / GCS — generic continuous or packetized */
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rfu-policy)RFU policy

BBFrame `reserved_future_use` bits are **emitted as 1** and
`reserved_zero_future_use` bits as **0**, following the DVB convention.
Parsers accept any value (no rejection on non-zero RFU) for forward
compatibility.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Two runnable examples ship with this crate (`cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example <name>`).

[§](https://docs.rs#parse_bbheader)`parse_bbheader`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Basic: parse a single DVB-S2 BBHEADER from raw bytes.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example parse_bbheader`
use dvb_bbframe::crc::crc8;
use dvb_bbframe::header::Bbheader;
fn main() {
    // A 10-byte Normal-Mode BBHEADER: MATYPE-1/2, UPL, DFL, SYNC, SYNCD, CRC-8.
    // (UPL=1520 bits = a 188-byte TS packet, SYNC=0x47, TS/CCM stream.)
    #[rustfmt::skip]
    let mut header = [
        0xD8, 0x00, // MATYPE-1, MATYPE-2
        0x05, 0xF0, // UPL = 1520 bits
        0xE0, 0x30, // DFL = 57392 bits
        0x47,       // SYNC byte
        0x00, 0x00, // SYNCD
        0x00,       // CRC-8 — filled below
    ];
    // In Normal Mode the MODE field is folded into the CRC-8: a stored byte
    // equal to crc8(header[..9]) decodes back to Mode::Normal.
    header[9] = crc8(&header[..9]);
    let hdr = Bbheader::parse(&header).expect("valid BBHEADER");
    println!("mode    : {:?}", hdr.mode);
    println!("ts_gs   : {:?}", hdr.matype.ts_gs);
    println!("ccm     : {}", hdr.matype.ccm);
    println!("issyi   : {}", hdr.matype.issyi);
    println!("UPL     : {} bits", hdr.upl);
    println!("DFL     : {} bits", hdr.dfl);
    println!("SYNC    : {:#04X}", hdr.sync);
    println!("SYNCD   : {}", hdr.syncd);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#walk_capture)`walk_capture`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
//! Advanced: walk a real DVB-S2 capture, reassemble BBFrames from TS private
//! sections, and parse every BBHEADER.
//!
//! Run with: `cargo run -p dvb-bbframe --example walk_capture`
//!
//! Reads the committed `tnt-5w-12732v-bbframe.ts` fixture at runtime, so the
//! example compiles even when the fixture is absent.
use dvb_bbframe::crc::crc8;
use dvb_bbframe::header::{Bbheader, Mode};
const BBFRAME_PID: u16 = 0x010E;
const NEW_FRAME_COUNT: u8 = 0xB8; // section count byte marking a new BBFrame
/// Reassemble complete BBFrames carried in TS private sections on `pid`.
fn extract_bbframes(data: &[u8], pid: u16) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    let mut current = Vec::with_capacity(8192);
    let mut started = false;
    for pkt in data.chunks(188) {
        if pkt.len() < 188 || pkt[0] != 0x47 {
            continue;
        }
        let ts_pid = ((u16::from(pkt[1]) & 0x1F) << 8) | u16::from(pkt[2]);
        if ts_pid != pid || pkt[3] & 0x30 != 0x10 {
            continue;
        }
        if pkt[4] != 0x00 || pkt[5] != 0x80 || pkt[6] != 0x00 {
            continue; // section header: 00 80 00 [slen] [count]
        }
        let slen = usize::from(pkt[7]);
        if slen == 0 || slen > 0xB4 {
            continue;
        }
        let data_end = 9 + (slen - 1);
        if data_end > 188 {
            continue;
        }
        if pkt[8] == NEW_FRAME_COUNT {
            if started && !current.is_empty() {
                frames.push(core::mem::take(&mut current));
            }
            started = true;
            current.clear();
        }
        if started {
            current.extend_from_slice(&pkt[9..data_end]);
        }
    }
    frames
}
fn main() {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/tests/fixtures/tnt-5w-12732v-bbframe.ts"
    );
    let data = match std::fs::read(path) {
        Ok(b) => b,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("fixture not available ({e}); nothing to do");
            return;
        }
    };
    let frames = extract_bbframes(&data, BBFRAME_PID);
    println!(
        "PID {BBFRAME_PID:#06X}: {} BBFrames reassembled",
        frames.len()
    );
    let mut normal = 0;
    let mut crc_ok = 0;
    for frame in &frames {
        if frame.len() < 10 {
            continue;
        }
        let hdr = Bbheader::parse(frame).expect("BBHEADER parses");
        if hdr.mode == Mode::Normal {
            normal += 1;
        }
        // NM integrity: stored CRC-8 equals computed over the first 9 bytes.
        if crc8(&frame[..9]) == frame[9] {
            crc_ok += 1;
        }
    }
    println!("Normal-Mode headers : {normal}");
    println!("CRC-8 intact        : {crc_ok}/{}", frames.len());
    if let Some(first) = frames.first() {
        let hdr = Bbheader::parse(first).unwrap();
        println!(
            "first frame         : UPL={} bits, DFL={} bits, SYNC={:#04X}",
            hdr.upl, hdr.dfl, hdr.sync
        );
    }
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [crc](https://docs.rs/crc/index.html)
- CRC-8 encoder per EN 302 755 Annex F / EN 302 307-1 §5.1.4.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error type for BBFrame parsing and serialization.
- [header](https://docs.rs/header/index.html)
- BBHEADER (Base-Band Header) parser and builder.
- [issy](https://docs.rs/issy/index.html)
- ISSY (Input Stream SYnchronizer) field decoding per EN 302 755 §5.1.7 / Annex C Table C.1 (DVB-T2) and EN 302 307-1 Annex D Table D.1 (DVB-S2 BUFSTAT).
- [packet](https://docs.rs/packet/index.html)
- User packet extraction from BBFrame data fields.
- [pump](https://docs.rs/pump/index.html)
- `BbframePump`
